cards.title: Use Shopify Search & Discovery for Filters and Recommendations
cards.summary: Replace paid filtering and recommendation apps with Shopify's free Search & Discovery app to manage filters, product recommendations and search.
cards.use_when: Setting up or cleaning up collection filters, upsell recommendations and on-site search results on a Shopify store.

cards.title: Reduce Apps and Image Weight to Protect Store Speed
cards.summary: Shopify handles a lot of performance work, but unused apps and oversized images are the practical levers you control.
cards.use_when: Diagnosing or preventing slow page loads after installing apps, changing themes, or uploading heavy product photography.

cards.title: Cover the Evergreen SEO Basics on Products, Collections and Store Settings
cards.summary: Set product, collection and store-level SEO fields properly, and keep publishing content as a trust signal for both search engines and AI agents.
cards.use_when: Completing baseline SEO for product pages, collection pages and the store homepage before or after launch.

cards.title: Match Checkout Branding to Your Store's Design System
cards.summary: Keep checkout colors consistent with the storefront, especially accent colors on buttons and error messages, so the buying step feels familiar.
cards.use_when: Styling the checkout page in the theme editor to keep the buying experience visually continuous with the storefront.

cards.title: Decide on Tipping, B2B Fields and Address Defaults at Checkout
cards.summary: Minor checkout settings — tipping, company name fields and address requirements — should be set deliberately based on the business model.
cards.use_when: Working through the full set of Shopify checkout settings on a new store setup or a settings audit.

cards.title: Install and Configure the Judge.me Review Widget on Product Pages
cards.summary: Install Judge.me review widgets on Shopify product pages, then gate visibility until you have a review base.
cards.use_when: Setting up social-proof tooling on your Shopify store's product pages (PDP) before or after launch.

cards.title: Set Up Automated Review Request Emails (Delays, Templates, Branding)
cards.summary: Configure Judge.me review-request emails with delays, branded templates, and moderation rules before requesting reviews.
cards.use_when: Building a post-purchase review collection flow to generate PDP social proof on a Shopify store.

cards.title: Enable Judge.me Features: Import Reviews, Product Groups, Widget Branding
cards.summary: Use Judge.me's import, product-grouping, and widget-customization features to maximize review coverage across your catalog.
cards.use_when: Consolidating existing reviews, de-duplicating proof across product variants, and branding review widgets.

cards.title: Create Shopify Markets for Multi-Country Selling
cards.summary: Set up Shopify Markets to give each country/region dedicated currency, catalog, language, and theme experiences from one dashboard.
cards.use_when: Expanding a Shopify store to sell internationally (e.g. a France-based store selling to Germany, Italy, the US).

cards.title: Adjust Prices and Catalog per Market
cards.summary: Use per-market catalogs and price adjustments to handle duties, positioning, and product availability by country.
cards.use_when: Setting country-specific pricing or excluding products for a specific Shopify market.

cards.title: Apply Market-Specific Theme Customizations
cards.summary: Change banners, layouts, and messages for specific Shopify markets without affecting the default store theme.
cards.use_when: Running an international store and showing country-specific banners, shipping messages, or holidays.

cards.title: Configure Taxes and Duties per Market
cards.summary: Set up country-level tax collection and duties in Shopify, with a preference for including taxes in listed prices rather than billing at checkout.
cards.use_when: Selling cross-border and deciding whether/how Shopify collects taxes by country.

cards.title: Add and Manage Warehouse Locations
cards.summary: Add physical warehouse locations in Shopify and assign inventory per location for accurate multi-warehouse fulfillment.
cards.use_when: Running multiple warehouses (e.g. one per region) and needing orders routed and inventory tracked correctly.

cards.title: Set Up Shipping Zones and Flat Rates per Country
cards.summary: Configure shipping zones and flat rates per country, offering free shipping above a threshold to reduce checkout abandonment.
cards.use_when: Setting up shipping and delivery for each country where your Shopify store sells.

cards.title: Add a Second Store Language with Translate & Adapt
cards.summary: Use Shopify's free Translate & Adapt app to add and auto-translate a second language, then refine and assign it to a market.
cards.use_when: Adding a second language (e.g. Arabic for KSA customers) to a Shopify store.

cards.title: Handle Currency Display When Shopify Payments Isn't Available
cards.summary: Understand the limitation of third-party currency apps when Shopify Payments can't be used, and pick a universally understood base currency.
cards.use_when: Selling internationally from a country where Shopify Payments isn't offered and needing multi-currency display.

cards.title: Choose and Set Up Payment Gateways by Market
cards.summary: Select the right mix of payment gateways per market, with Shopify Payments as the preferred default when available.
cards.use_when: Setting up checkout payment options, especially for international or multi-market stores.

cards.title: Manage Orders and Fulfillment Notifications
cards.summary: Understand how orders flow from Shopify to warehouses and how notifications and tracking are handled.
cards.use_when: Setting up fulfillment after launch, whether with a warehouse integration or manual shipping.

cards.title: Run Real Test Orders Across All Locations Before Launch
cards.summary: Verify shipping, payments, taxes, and warehouse fulfillment by placing real test orders in every market/warehouse before going live.
cards.use_when: Pre-launch checklist for a Shopify store, especially multi-warehouse or high-SKU stores.

cards.title: Set Order ID Format and Order Processing Preferences
cards.summary: Configure Shopify's order ID extension and order processing settings so customers see an order summary before paying.
cards.use_when: Finalizing checkout/order settings before launch on a Shopify store.

cards.title: Order ID and order-processing settings to configure at launch
cards.summary: Which Shopify general order settings to keep at default and how the order ID prefix/suffix helps hide store volume.
cards.use_when: Initial store setup or a settings audit for cart/checkout and fulfillment workflow before launch.

cards.title: Configure Shopify customer notifications without breaking checkout emails
cards.summary: Which default Shopify notifications matter most, when each is triggered, and why you should barely edit the HTML.
cards.use_when: Notification and post-purchase communication setup for order confirmations, shipping updates and draft orders.

cards.title: Set up customer support before launch, not after
cards.summary: Staffing, tooling and policy choices that keep incoming order and shipping tickets from turning buyers into angry former customers.
cards.use_when: Preparing customer support capacity and response workflow ahead of a launch or high-volume sales period.

cards.title: Read conversion-rate funnel breakdowns to find where buyers drop
cards.summary: Using the Shopify conversion-rate breakdown to separate traffic, product-page, cart and checkout problems.
cards.use_when: Diagnosing a weak conversion rate or deciding whether the problem sits in merchandising, PDP, cart or checkout.

cards.title: Choose the analytics time window and comparison before drawing conclusions
cards.summary: Why Shopify analytics require a long window and an explicit comparison period to mean anything.
cards.use_when: Any recurring analytics review, launch post-mortem or monthly performance meeting.

cards.title: Customize the Shopify analytics dashboard around your own metrics
cards.summary: How to rearrange, add and save reports so the dashboard reflects what you actually manage.
cards.use_when: Setting up recurring reporting for a store you operate or manage, especially when the default dashboard hides the metrics you act on.

cards.title: Use the customer cohort/retention report to time win-back emails
cards.summary: Reading retention month-by-month to learn when customers return and when to trigger reactivation.
cards.use_when: Planning retention and email reactivation timing for a store with at least several months of order history.

cards.title: Ask Shopify's AI agent for custom analytics reports
cards.summary: Using Shopify's built-in AI exploration and Sidekick to generate reports without building them manually.
cards.use_when: Producing a quick custom report (e.g. multi-year conversion trend) without manually constructing charts in the reports library.

cards.title: Read the sales breakdown and by-channel metrics correctly
cards.summary: Interpreting gross sales, net sales, discounts, channel attribution and AOV before acting on them.
cards.use_when: Monthly performance review, channel-mix decisions or pricing/discount evaluation.

cards.title: Don't rely on default Shopify emails to fix weak product pages
cards.summary: Using post-purchase and support signals to detect product-page and policy gaps rather than patching them with notifications.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether to expand shipping policies, FAQ content or PDP copy after launch based on incoming support tickets.

cards.title: Initializing a Shopify account and choosing a store name
cards.summary: Set up a Shopify account email and store name with the understanding that the myshopify.com handle is permanent and the display name is editable.
cards.use_when: You are starting a brand-new store from scratch and need to create the Shopify account and store identity.

cards.title: Setting up Shopify Payments with exact legal identity match
cards.summary: Enter legal names, addresses and business details in Shopify Payments exactly as they appear on government IDs so payouts are not held.
cards.use_when: You are enabling payment capture for the first time and need payouts to clear without verification holds.

cards.title: Defining physical presence for tax collection
cards.summary: Configure the physical presence (nexus) location so Shopify collects tax only where you are legally required, avoiding over- and under-collection.
cards.use_when: You are configuring tax regions and need Shopify to calculate the correct rate at checkout.

cards.title: Building shipping zones for domestic and international delivery
cards.summary: Create separate shipping zones for domestic and international destinations and set rates for each so checkout quotes realistic delivery costs.
cards.use_when: You are about to sell to customers outside your home country and need shipping rates that do not undercharge or block checkout.

cards.title: Setting default package weights so calculated rates do not undercharge
cards.summary: Enter default package empty weights in the shipping profile so carrier-calculated rates reflect real shipping cost instead of light parcels.
cards.use_when: You use carrier-calculated or weight-based shipping rates and are worried about undercharging on multi-item orders.

cards.title: Connecting a custom domain and a business email address
cards.summary: Link a purchased custom domain to the Shopify store and set up a matching branded email so the store is reachable and correspondence is credible.
cards.use_when: You have bought a domain and need it pointed at the store and a matching email set up before launch.

cards.title: Testing checkout, tax and policy links with test mode transactions
cards.summary: Place simulated orders in Shopify Payments test mode to confirm checkout, tax calculation and policy links actually work before you remove the store password.
cards.use_when: You are one step from launching and need evidence that payments, tax and legal links function end to end.

cards.title: Installing tracking and verifying it fires before launch
cards.summary: Add analytics and pixel tracking to the store and confirm events actually fire so conversion measurement is not empty after launch.
cards.use_when: You are installing analytics or ad pixels and need to confirm data will be captured once the store is live.

cards.title: Publishing required legal and policy pages before removing the password
cards.summary: Create the policy and contact pages a store needs, then confirm they are linked and readable, because a password gate hides missing pages until launch day.
cards.use_when: You are preparing for launch and need the legal, policy and contact pages in place and linked.

cards.title: Doing store setup in the right order to avoid launch breakage
cards.summary: Sequence Shopify setup so identity, payments, tax, shipping, domain and tracking are configured before testing and removing the password gate.
cards.use_when: You are planning the launch sequence and want to avoid discovering broken checkout or tax settings after customers arrive.

cards.title: Verifying each setup step actually worked
cards.summary: Close out each store configuration step with a concrete check, because a saved setting is not proof that checkout, tax or links behave correctly.
cards.use_when: You have configured a store section such as payments, shipping or domains and want to confirm it works before relying on it.

cards.title: Configure Shopify Legal Business Name and Address Before Anything Else
cards.summary: Set the store's legal business name and address in Settings > General immediately after account creation, since payments, taxes and shipping defaults inherit these details.
cards.use_when: Right after creating a new Shopify store and before setting up payments, shipping or taxes.

cards.title: Add First Products with Descriptive Titles, Weight and Dimensions
cards.summary: Enter product title, description, media, price, inventory, weight and location because weight and dimensions are required inputs for calculated shipping later.
cards.use_when: Adding the first products to a new store before building collections or shipping rates.

cards.title: Organize Products into Manual or Smart Collections for Findability
cards.summary: Use collections to group products so customers find what they want quickly, which the source links to higher likelihood of completing a purchase.
cards.use_when: Merchandising a product catalog so shoppers can navigate to relevant groups from the homepage and navigation.

cards.title: Choose and Customize a Shopify Theme, Then Restyle It
cards.summary: Pick a theme through the theme editor and use Sidekick to generate color palettes, font pairings and layout direction instead of designing from scratch.
cards.use_when: Designing the visual layer of a new store before launch, after products and collections exist.

cards.title: Set Up Navigation Menus with Nested Submenus
cards.summary: Build an intuitive menu structure with nested submenus so a first-time visitor can reach any product group in a few clicks.
cards.use_when: Configuring store navigation after products, collections and pages exist, so menu links point to real destinations.

cards.title: Connect or Buy a Domain and Set It as Primary
cards.summary: Connect an existing domain or buy one through Shopify, then test that it loads the store and set it as the primary domain instead of the myshopify.com address.
cards.use_when: Giving the store a real URL before launch so customers, email and search treat it as the canonical address.

cards.title: Enable Two-Step Authentication Before Activating Shopify Payments
cards.summary: Two-step authentication is required for Shopify Payments, so turn it on and store recovery codes securely before starting payment verification.
cards.use_when: Preparing to activate payments on a new store — this is a gating requirement, not an optional security nicety.

cards.title: Activate Shopify Payments with Exact Legal Names to Avoid Verification Holds
cards.summary: Choose the correct business type and enter legal names exactly as they appear on government-issued ID, because mismatches are the top cause of verification delays.
cards.use_when: Setting up Shopify Payments so the store can actually accept money, especially for solo founders or registered companies.

cards.title: Set Payment Capture, Wallets and Customer Contact Defaults
cards.summary: Configure automatic capture at checkout, confirm express wallets are enabled, and set customer contact and marketing consent options.
cards.use_when: Finalizing checkout behavior on a new store after Shopify Payments is activated.

cards.title: Build Shipping Zones and Rates Without Undercharging
cards.summary: Configure domestic and international zones with rates or calculated shipping, and be deliberate about flat rate, pass-through or shipping built into product price.
cards.use_when: Setting up shipping so orders go out and shipping charges cover real carrier costs.

cards.title: Add a New Shipping Zone to a Specific Country
cards.summary: Remove the target country from the international zone first, then create a market and assign its own rates, because a country can only live in one zone at a time.
cards.use_when: Expanding shipping to a specific country or region with rates distinct from the default international zone.

cards.title: Set Default Package Weights and Dimensions to Prevent Shipping Undercharges
cards.summary: Create packages with accurate outside dimensions and empty-package weight so calculated shipping rates reflect the packed box, not just the product.
cards.use_when: Any store using calculated shipping, before launch, to stop quietly losing money on every order.

cards.title: Configure Local Delivery, Store Pickup and Shipping Labels with Billing Thresholds
cards.summary: Set local delivery radius or postcodes and pickup times, then understand that label costs are billed to your Shopify account rather than deducted from customer payments.
cards.use_when: Serving local customers or handling fulfillment in-house, and reconciling where shipping label charges appear financially.

cards.title: Review Shipping Insurance Coverage Before High-Value Shipments
cards.summary: Insurance is included automatically on some plans but not others, has exclusions, and can also be bought from carriers, third-party apps or self-insured.
cards.use_when: Deciding how to handle lost or damaged shipments of fragile or high-value products.

cards.title: Set Up a Repeatable Fulfillment Workflow with Bulk Processing
cards.summary: Define the order path from review to packing slip to label to fulfilled status, and use bulk actions when order volume picks up.
cards.use_when: Preparing fulfillment operations before orders arrive so the process is repeatable rather than improvised.

cards.title: Publish Return and Refund Policies and Enable Self-Serve Returns
cards.summary: Insert Shopify's policy template, edit it, publish it, and turn on self-serve returns while defining return window, shipping cost and restocking terms.
cards.use_when: Launching a store that needs clear returns terms visible at checkout and a low-friction returns process.

cards.title: Configure Sales Tax Based on Physical Presence and Set Duties for International Markets
cards.summary: Tax settings should reflect where the business has physical presence, and Shopify then calculates sales tax and duties at checkout for configured regions.
cards.use_when: Making the store legally collect tax at checkout before launch, including for international customers.

cards.title: Run Test Orders in Shopify Payments Test Mode Before Launch
cards.summary: Use test mode with official test card numbers to verify checkout, tax calculations, shipping rates, fulfillment workflow and policy links — including on mobile — before turning test mode off.
cards.use_when: Final pre-launch verification after payments, shipping, tax and fulfillment are all configured.

cards.title: Run a Pre-Launch Audit of Products, Policies and Navigation
cards.summary: Use Sidekick to scan for missing descriptions, prices and images, generate required policy pages, then do a final click-through of the store as a first-time visitor.
cards.use_when: Final quality pass before removing password protection, when the builder has been staring at the store too long to spot obvious errors.

cards.title: Remove Password Protection to Go Live and Announce Launch
cards.summary: Launch by deselecting password protection in online store preferences, then drive the first visits with a personal email and a structured social post sequence.
cards.use_when: The day the store has passed verification and is ready to receive real customers.

cards.title: Use Campaigns and UTM Automatch Rules to Attribute Marketing in Shopify
cards.summary: Create named campaigns, group traffic with UTM automatch rules, and read results through the attribution models that match the question you are asking.
cards.use_when: Measuring which channels and campaigns actually drive sessions and orders, so budget and creative decisions are based on data rather than guesswork.

cards.title: Choose a Shopify attribution model by marketing goal
cards.summary: Use the five Shopify attribution models to assign credit to the right touchpoints based on whether you're measuring awareness, mid-journey support, or final conversion.
cards.use_when: Deciding how to judge which traffic source or campaign is driving purchases before reallocating ad budget or cutting a channel.

cards.title: Set up campaign tracking activities and a morning marketing report
cards.summary: Add campaign activities by channel or UTM parameter so traffic appears in campaign reports, and pull a daily marketing summary instead of digging manually.
cards.use_when: You are running multiple channels and need a repeatable way to see which source is driving sessions and sales each day.

cards.title: Set up marketing automations for welcome, cart recovery and lifecycle messages
cards.summary: Use Shopify's pre-built automation templates (or Shopify Flow) to send email, SMS and push messages on triggers without manual sends.
cards.use_when: You want welcome discounts, abandoned cart recovery, post-purchase upsells, win-back or thank-you messages running without sending each one by hand.

cards.title: Use Shopify Messaging campaigns within the free email allowance
cards.summary: Create and send branded email campaigns from the Shopify admin, using templates, dynamic product blocks and free monthly email volume before paying for an app.
cards.use_when: Sending announcements, newsletters, product highlights or promotions to your contact list and deciding whether you need a paid email platform.

cards.title: Build targeted customer segments for email and offers
cards.summary: Create behavior-based segments so campaigns and discounts target the right customers instead of the whole list.
cards.use_when: Sending a campaign, scheduling a promotion, or restricting a discount code to specific buyers such as repeat customers or high spenders.

cards.title: Connect Meta (Facebook/Instagram) and TikTok to Shopify before running ads
cards.summary: Install the sales-channel apps and complete business verification so paid ads actually track and route traffic to your store.
cards.use_when: Launching your first paid social ads to drive immediate traffic to a new store.

cards.title: Run an organic social content mix with clear paths to purchase
cards.summary: Post 3–4 times a week with varied content types and make every post route people to the store.
cards.use_when: Building sustainable traffic and community on Instagram, Facebook or TikTok without relying only on paid ads.

cards.title: Vet Shopify apps before installing
cards.summary: Screen apps by rating, review count, recency of reviews, developer track record and Built for Shopify badge, and install one at a time.
cards.use_when: Adding any app — email/SMS, reviews, pop-ups, referrals — to your store and deciding which one to trust.

cards.title: Match app choices to the marketing job you need done
cards.summary: Pick apps by the specific gap — email scale, SMS, reviews, pop-ups, referrals — and avoid overlapping tools.
cards.use_when: You have outgrown built-in Shopify messaging or need SMS, review collection, pop-up capture or a referral program.

cards.title: Find your largest funnel drop-off with the conversion rate breakdown report
cards.summary: Use Shopify's conversion rate breakdown to locate the biggest leak between sessions, add-to-cart, checkout and purchase.
cards.use_when: Traffic is steady but purchases are low and you need to know which funnel stage to fix first.

cards.title: Fix product pages: visuals, descriptions, trust signals and CTA
cards.summary: Address the common conversion killers on product pages — weak images, generic descriptions, mismatched price-to-value, missing reviews or murky returns — with specific fixes.
cards.use_when: Your biggest funnel drop is before add-to-cart, or product pages get traffic but don't convert.

cards.title: Reduce navigation friction with click depth, clear categories and mega menus
cards.summary: Keep products reachable in 2–3 clicks, name categories in plain language, and use mega menus and breadcrumbs on larger catalogs.
cards.use_when: Shoppers can't find products, bounce out of category pages, or you're structuring a menu for a growing catalog.

cards.title: Improve site search with predictive text and synonyms
cards.summary: Enable predictive search and add synonyms for misspellings and alternative terms so shoppers find products using their own words.
cards.use_when: Shoppers search and get no results, or you sell products with regional/alternative names (e.g. sneakers vs trainers).

cards.title: Diagnose and reduce site speed problems
cards.summary: Use bounce rate and PageSpeed Insights to find speed problems, then cut unused apps, compress images and replace heavy theme elements.
cards.use_when: Your bounce rate looks high, mobile pages load slowly, or conversions feel capped despite traffic.

cards.title: Cut checkout friction: payment options, forms and cost transparency
cards.summary: Reduce the checkout drop by enabling accelerated payments, guest checkout, minimal form fields and early shipping cost visibility.
cards.use_when: The largest funnel drop is between cart/checkout and completed purchase, or abandoned cart rates look high.

cards.title: Build checkout trust with badges and concrete delivery dates
cards.summary: Add secure-checkout signals and specific delivery estimates to reduce last-step hesitation.
cards.use_when: Checkout is where buyers hesitate, or you want clearer expectations to reduce 'where is my order' friction and abandonment.

cards.title: Set up abandoned cart and abandonment recovery flows
cards.summary: Recover lost buyers with a default abandoned checkout email, a cart-abandonment automation, and optional WhatsApp recovery for higher-value carts.
cards.use_when: Customers add to cart or reach checkout then leave without buying, and you want automated recovery without manual outreach.

cards.title: Run a VIP campaign using top products, a segment and an exclusive code
cards.summary: Personalize offers to loyal customers instead of discounting the whole list, using a repeatable workflow of bestsellers, a VIP segment and a targeted code.
cards.use_when: You want to reward repeat buyers and protect margin instead of sending a blanket discount to everyone.
